title: Committee of Supply – Head O (Ministry of Health)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head O (Ministry of Health)

sections.label: Bringing care closer to home
sections.summary: The speaker called for MOH to bring care and subsidy closer to less mobile patients, noting progress in access and home palliative care financing.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: In 2022, I called for the Ministry of Health (MOH) to look at how care can be brought closer to home for patients, especially for residents who are less mobile, who find it more difficult to get to clinics.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: In short, bring subsidy to where the patient is, if the policy intent is to support the care where the patient is.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: There has been progress in the years since then, improved access, also better financing support for palliative care at home, which is important for residents who are terminally ill, where time is even more precious than before, and where being at home in their last weeks and months is deeply important.

sections.label: MediSave for outpatient scans
sections.summary: The passage asks whether MOH can be more flexible with the use of MediSave for outpatient scans.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Can MOH be more flexible with the use of MediSave for outpatient scans?

sections.label: Polyclinic online bookings reserved quickly
sections.summary: Residents wrote to the speaker that polyclinic online bookings open at 10.00 pm and get reserved within minutes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: I have had Clementi residents, but even residents staying in the east of Singapore, writing to me to share about these challenges.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: They find that when the bookings open at 10.00 pm, in the case of some polyclinic systems, the online bookings get "choped", get reserved, very quickly within a few minutes.

sections.label: Portable subsidy vouchers for seniors
sections.summary: The speaker filed a Parliamentary Question asking MOH to consider portable subsidy vouchers for seniors facing digital booking challenges.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: The systems made it harder for these seniors.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: And I have met elderly residents who tell me when they show up at the polyclinic without an appointment, sometimes they get turned away, asked to go online to make a booking, even though they do not know how to go online.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: In 2024, I filed a Parliamentary Question (PQ) to MOH.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: I asked MOH to consider portable subsidy vouchers to help underwrite some of the cost difference between polyclinic care and private GP care, especially for seniors who may physically live right next to the polyclinic, nearby the polyclinic, but who due to digital challenges, find it very hard to go online to book an appointment for the next day at the polyclinic.

sections.label: Coordinating doctor for complex patients
sections.summary: The passage asks whether a coordinating doctor supported by specialists could wrap care around patients with complex needs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: That tells you that at the highest levels of Government, we recognise coordination is an important role and adds value beyond a single specialisation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: So, for patients with multiple complex medical conditions, can there be a coordinating doctor supported by different specialists from medical, nursing, allied health, also with adequate admin support, so we can wrap care around the patient with complex needs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: In a previous PQ that I filed, MOH shared that just before the COVID-19 pandemic in 2019, there were 7,000 Singaporeans a year, with 24 or more specialist outpatient clinic visits in a year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: In the year 2019, there were over 2,000 Singaporeans who had 36 or more outpatient clinic visits to a specialist clinic in a year, three or more visits per month on average.

sections.label: Improving healthcare IT for frontliners
sections.summary: The passage asks MOH what is being done to improve healthcare IT to help frontliners, including junior doctors.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Healthcare workers, patients trying to navigate systems and computers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: So, can MOH tell us what is being done to improve healthcare IT to help frontliners, including our junior doctors?

sections.label: Fertility support for young cancer patients
sections.summary: Proposes front-loading Government funding for young cancer patients needing fertility support and exploring interest-free loans with financial institutions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Second, front load Government funding for young cancer patients needing fertility support, because a MediSave-based model does not work so well when the patient is too young to have earned MediSave from working and when the patient's family might not have much MediSave, if the family is starting with less.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Third, work with financial institutions to see if we can have interest-free loans to support young cancer patients needing fertility preservation.

sections.label: Rare Disease Fund matching grant
sections.summary: The Government later set up a Rare Disease Fund with three-to-one matching grant for public donations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: The Government later set up a Rare Disease Fund with three-to-one matching grant for public donations.

sections.label: Regulator and broader Government spending
sections.summary: Argues the visible hand of the regulator is needed for fairer insurance decisions, and Government spending must consider broader societal impact.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: In short, as I said five years ago in Parliament, sometimes the invisible hand of the market becomes unbalanced.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: And that is why we need the visible hand of the regulator to re-shape insurance behaviour and ensure proportionate, fair and more reasonable decisions on insurance for young Singaporeans who have gone through a mental health situation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Second, Government spending must look not just at a single item on a budget, but the broader impact to society, because sometimes, spending on coordination of care becomes an enabler, a catalyst to help a family, and sometimes save a breadwinner's job.

sections.label: MOH junior doctors work hours guideline
sections.summary: MOH stated in Parliament on 10 January 2024 that junior doctors' total weekly work hours should not exceed 80 when averaged monthly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: MOH has mentioned on 10 January 2024 in Parliament, that their guideline for junior doctors stipulates that, when average out over a month, the total work hours per week of junior doctors should not exceed 80 hours.

sections.label: Junior doctors hours versus employment guidelines
sections.summary: A 2023 survey reports junior doctors average 71 hours a week, compared with MOM's 44 contractual hours and 72 monthly overtime hours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A nationwide survey published in the Journal of the Academy of Medicine Singapore, in 2023, reports that junior doctors work an average of 71 hours a week, which adds up to 284 hours on an average month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In contrast, the Ministry of Manpower's (MOM's) employment guidelines stipulates that the contractual hours of work for common work arrangement under part four of the Employment Act is 44 hours a week and a typical employee is only allowed to work up to 72 overtime hours a month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Any more would presumably not be healthy for the employee.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This suggests that MOH allows junior doctors to work 72 hours more than what is usually deemed healthy for a typical employee.

sections.label: Medical errors and clinical hours correlation
sections.summary: The same survey found a significant correlation between the number of medical errors made and additional clinical hours worked per week.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The same survey mentioned earlier found a significant correlation between the number of medical errors made with the amount of additional clinical hours worked per week.

sections.label: Healthier SG clinic enrolment numbers
sections.summary: Asks how many of about 1,600 GP clinics have voluntarily become Healthier SG clinics and enrolment percentages by age segment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: One, what is the latest number, out of about 1,600 GP clinics in which focus on primary care, that have voluntarily become a Healthier SG clinic?

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Two, what are the percentages of Singaporeans who have enrolled in Healthier SG in each of these age segments: between (a) 40- and 49-years-old; (b) 50- and 59-years-old; (c) 60- and 69-years-old; (d) 70- and 79-years-old; and lastly, (e) above 80-years-old.

sections.label: Healthier SG budget disbursement
sections.summary: Asks how much of the estimated $200 million annual Healthier SG budget was disbursed to GP clinics in 2024.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Five, more than one year into implementation, how much of the estimated $200 million annual budget for Healthier SG that has been disbursed to GP clinics in either calendar year or financial year 2024, and how much goes to GPs in (a) service fees earned per enrolled patient; (b) information technology (IT) grants to help enhance their Clinic Management Systems to better link up with MOH's Healthier SG systems; and (c) additional clinic administrative costs to coordinate with partners like HPB in their GPs' prescription?

sections.label: Senior care and retirement housing models
sections.summary: Asks MOH's views on private operators' interest in retirement villages and homes and nursing home licensing concerns.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In September 2023, MOH launched the Shared Stay-in Senior Care Services sandbox to explore the feasibility of having a foreign live-in caregiver to help care for several seniors in one apartment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Two, for seniors with mild to moderate ageing needs but cannot or do not want to be living alone or cared for in their own homes anymore, what are MOH's views on private operators' (a) interests in developing other new models like retirement villages and retirement homes, common in European countries which are also facing fast ageing population; and (b) the private operators' feedback that the current nursing homes licensing regime is too onerous, costly to comply with and the licence tenure of two years too short, to give certainty to operate with financial sustainability for such potential retirement villages and homes; and (c) their concerns that dependencies on high MOH subsidies for seniors like those in the nursing homes currently will continue to increase healthcare costs exponentially in fast-ageing Singapore?

sections.label: Malay and Indian traditional medicines
sections.summary: Asks whether MOH sees wisdom in beginning studies into traditional medicines of the Malay and Indian communities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As multiracialism and multiculturalism are unique strengths of Singapore, I have also taken an interest in the traditional medicines and therapeutic practices passed down through generations among our Malay community, like the concept of semangat, herbal remedies and urut.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
sentences.text: For our Indian community, there are what we call Ayurveda, Yoga, Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha and Homoeopathy (AYUSH), which is increasingly known in India.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
sentences.text: My question is, does MOH sees wisdom in beginning studies and understanding into such traditional medicines of our Malay and Indian communities too?

sections.label: Fundamental healthcare challenge remains
sections.summary: States that despite government initiatives to review MediSave, enhance CareShield and improve palliative care and caregiver support, the fundamental challenge remains.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: While I recognise the Government's initiatives to review MediSave, enhance CareShield and improve palliative care and caregiver support, the fundamental challenge remains.

sections.label: CareShield Life payout adequacy
sections.summary: Asks whether CareShield Life payouts are keeping pace with soaring costs of nursing homes, home-based care and assisted living.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Are CareShield Life payouts keeping pace with the soaring costs of nursing homes, home-based care and assisted living?

sections.label: MediSave limits for seniors
sections.summary: Fewer than three in 10 eligible seniors reached the $300 annual limit in 2023, and some residents say MediSave caps are insufficient.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Fewer than three in 10 eligible seniors reached the $300 annual limit in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Similarly, the $200 monthly MediSave Care limit for severe disabilities may fall short of long-term care needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Some residents have also raised concerns that the $600 annual cap on MediSave use for health insurance premiums is insufficient.

sections.label: Three frontier policy domains
sections.summary: The speaker names adult education, social mobility and long-term healthcare as frontier policy domains, with long-term care needs growing due to ageing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Well, in my mind, there are also three frontier policy domains that will transform our social support system for Singaporeans going forward.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: They are: adult education, social mobility and long-term healthcare.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: For long-term care, our needs will only grow sharply because of our ageing population, longer lifespans but not necessarily healthspans, and changing family structures.

sections.label: Long-term care fee cap questions
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether a fee cap framework could apply to long-term care and whether subsidy and grant dates could be brought forward.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Second, taking a leaf from the fee cap framework that has been in effect for the preschool sector, would the Ministry consider a fee cap framework as well for the long-term care sector?

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Third, on the enhanced subsidies for long-term care services and the Home Caregiver Grant, can the effective dates be brought forward to bring earlier relief to Singaporeans?

sections.label: Higher outpatient withdrawal limits
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Government to set higher outpatient withdrawal limits for older Singaporeans and adjust them annually for healthcare cost inflation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It is beneficial for outpatient treatment to be sought early before conditions deteriorate and hospitalisation becomes necessary.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I urge the Government to set higher outpatient withdrawal limits for older Singaporeans and adjust them annually to keep up with healthcare cost inflation.

sections.label: MediSave dental coverage limits
sections.summary: MediSave generally does not cover dental treatments unless they involve surgery and are medically necessary, so non-surgical procedures are not claimable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: MediSave generally does not cover dental treatments unless they involve surgery and are medically necessary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Non-surgical procedures like extractions, crowns, dentures and braces are not MediSave claimable.

sections.label: Project Silver Screen oral checks
sections.summary: About 13% of over 60-year-olds are completely toothless, and MOH launched Project Silver Screen in 2018 to provide functional screening including oral health checks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: About 13% of over 60-year-olds are completely toothless.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: MOH launched Project Silver Screen in 2018 to provide functional screening, including oral health checks, for seniors aged 60 and above.

sections.label: Dental subsidies and MediSave coverage
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Ministry to review dental subsidies, expand MediSave coverage and integrate dental care into Healthier SG.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Preventive dental care should be encouraged to reduce these long-term health risks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I urge the Ministry to review how dental subsidies are structured, expand MediSave coverage for essential treatments and integrate dental care into Healthier SG.

sections.label: CHAS card and dental subsidies
sections.summary: The speaker urges MOH to extend subsidies for preventive dental procedures at private clinics to ease Government clinic waiting times.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Many residents share their frustrations, including Nanyang residents, that the orange Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS) card offers little benefit for private dental treatments while Government dental clinics face months-long waiting times.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: To ease the burden on Government clinics and improve accessibility, I urge MOH to extend subsidies for preventive dental procedures at private clinics.

sections.label: Grants for overseas dental students
sections.summary: The speaker urges MOH to consider pre-employment grants for overseas dental students from good universities abroad.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: With an ageing population and growing demand for dental care, this is a missed opportunity to attract talent back to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: I urge MOH to consider offering pre-employment grants to overseas dental students from good universities abroad.

sections.label: Tighter controls on vaping imports
sections.summary: The speaker urges MOH to work with MHA, Police and CNB to tighten controls on illegal vaping imports and enforce stricter penalties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: To address this, I urge MOH to collaborate closely with the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), including the Police and Central Narcotics Bureau (CNB), to tighten controls on illegal imports of vaping products and enforce stricter penalties against offenders.

sections.label: Regulating the psychology profession
sections.summary: The speaker says it is time for MOH to regulate the psychology profession to protect vulnerable individuals and ensure professionalism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Vulnerable individuals seeking help deserve to be protected from unqualified practitioners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: So, to ensure high standards of professionalism and safeguards, it is time for MOH to regulate the psychology profession.

sections.label: Mental health access and recovery rates
sections.summary: The National Mental Health Office tracks access indicators, and the UK study and recovery target are cited.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The National Mental Health Office has committed to tracking indicators measuring access to mental healthcare, such as medium treatment delay for common mental disorders.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: A United Kingdom (UK) study of nearly 40,000 patients from 2010 to 2013 found that an above-average therapist can achieve a recovery rate of above 80% over 16 sessions, instead of close to 0% for a below-average therapist.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The UK has also set a recovery rate target of 50% for all mental health services.

sections.label: Tracking mental care quality indicators
sections.summary: The question asks how the National Mental Health Office will track indicators on quality of mental care, including recovery and deterioration rates.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: First, how will the National Mental Health Office track indicators relating to the quality of mental care, which should include recovery rates and deterioration rates?

sections.label: Gaps in women's health research
sections.summary: The passage states gaps remain in autoimmune disorders and mental health, where women are more affected but most pre-clinical treatment studies were done on men.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Apart from reacting differently to medication and vaccines, there remains significant gaps in areas, such as autoimmune disorders, which affect women more; and also mental health, where, for example, women are more likely to suffer from post-traumatic stress disorder, but most pre-clinical studies on treatment were done on men.

sections.label: National Mental Health Strategy reception
sections.summary: The question asks about reception and adoption of the National Mental Health and Wellbeing Strategy and National Mental Health Office, and the Office's initiatives and future plans.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The National Mental Health and Wellbeing Strategy and National Mental Health Office were launched to improve coordination and access to mental health services.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: How have the reception and adoption of the strategy been so far and what initiatives has the Office undertaken, and what can we expect from the Office moving forward?

sections.label: Regulating psychologists and private counsellors
sections.summary: The question asks how MOH ensures digital outlets provide real professional human support, and calls for distinguishing psychologists from private counsellors and considering formal regulations and consumer protection.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: How is MOH ensuring that the digital space outlet remains one that provides real professional human support?

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: We need to distinguish between psychologists and private counsellors and start considering formal regulations for psychologists and strict consumer protection measures for private counselling services.

sections.label: Strategy for children's healthy lifestyles
sections.summary: The strategy aims to help children eat, sleep, learn, exercise and bond well through purposeful screen use, a Health Plan for every child and enhanced school support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The strategy aims to help our children eat well, sleep well, learn well, exercise well and to bond well to support and reinforce healthy lifestyles through purposeful screen use, a Health Plan for every child and enhanced support for schools.

sections.label: Receptiveness of Grow Well SG
sections.summary: The question asks MOH to share the receptiveness of Grow Well SG thus far.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, can MOH share what has been the receptiveness of Grow Well SG thus far?

sections.label: Seniors' mental health and subsidies
sections.summary: The speaker highlighted seniors' and caregivers' well-being, social isolation, loneliness and dementia, and welcomed subsidies and expanded public healthcare capacity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: During last year’s Motion on Advancing Mental Health, I highlighted the need to address seniors’ and caregivers’ well-being, particularly social isolation, loneliness and dementia.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: I also called for better insurance coverage and subsidies, and welcome the assurance of up to 80% subsidies at public institutions and ongoing efforts to expand public healthcare capacity.

sections.label: Expanding teams' reach and awareness
sections.summary: The passage asks how the reach and public awareness of over 70 island-wide teams can be expanded.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: With over 70 teams island-wide, how can we expand their reach and public awareness?

sections.label: Project Hayat suicide prevention recommendations
sections.summary: The working group for Project Hayat presented recommendations for a national suicide prevention strategy, per the S.A.V.E.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The working group for Project Hayat presented its recommendations for a national suicide prevention strategy, per the S.A.V.E.

sections.label: Suicide reduction KPIs for office
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the National Mental Health Office will establish KPIs specific to reducing the number of suicides.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Will the National Mental Health Office establish KPIs specific to seeing a reduction in the number of suicides?

sections.label: Well-Being Circles and people supported
sections.summary: The Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth updated that there were 12 Well-Being Circles and more than 3,000 people supported.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In last year's COS debate, the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth updated that there were 12 Well-Being Circles as part of the SG Mental Well-Being Network and more than 3,000 people have been supported.

sections.label: Delivery costs by residency status
sections.summary: At KK Women's and Children's Hospital, a normal C class ward delivery costs Singaporeans $1,390, PRs $2,870, and non-residents more than $8,000.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: At KK Women's and Children's Hospital, a normal delivery in a C class ward cost Singaporean mothers $1,390, which is fully MediSave covered.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Permanent Residents (PRs) pay $2,870, with most of it MediSave claimable and $120 being payable in cash.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Non-resident mothers must pay more than $8,000, claiming less than $3,000 from MediSave and paying about $5,300 in cash.

sections.label: Foreign mother family incomes
sections.summary: The 2019 SG LEED study found foreign mother families have the lowest per capita income and 17% of foreign mothers held Long-Term Visit Passes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The 2019 SG LEED study found that these families have the lowest per capita income at about $1,700 compared to citizen couples at about $2,600 and citizen mother, foreign father families at $3,100.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Furthermore, 17% of foreign mothers with Singaporean children still held a Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP), despite being married for an average of eight years.

sections.label: Ageing population healthcare spending
sections.summary: An ageing population, medical advancements and complex care make managing healthcare spend challenging, and healthcare may soon be the largest Government expenditure.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: An ageing population, coupled with medical advancements and the increasing complexity of care, managing healthcare spend is exceedingly challenging, and healthcare may soon become the largest Government expenditure.

sections.label: Shorter-term cost efficiencies achieved
sections.summary: The passage asks what level of shorter-term cost efficiencies has been achieved from current efforts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: What level of shorter-term cost efficiencies have been achieved from current efforts?

sections.label: Optimal public-private healthcare mix
sections.summary: The passage asks what optimal public-private mix best serves people's needs and keeps healthcare costs sustainable.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: What is the optimal public-private mix that best serves the needs of our people and keeps healthcare costs sustainable?

sections.label: Mental health service wait times
sections.summary: The passage states that wait times for mental health services remain long.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Wait times for mental health services remain long.

sections.label: Mental health and Healthier SG
sections.summary: The passage states that mental health is yet to be integrated in Healthier SG.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Mental health is yet to be integrated in Healthier SG.

sections.label: Ophthalmologist declares private practice interest
sections.summary: The speaker declares an interest as an ophthalmologist in private practice.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Chairman, I declare my interest as an ophthalmologist in private practice.

sections.label: Healthcare insurance premium growth
sections.summary: Healthcare insurance premiums grew 13.7% in 2022, 12% in 2024, and are projected to grow another 12% this year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The knock-on effect is seen in the cost of healthcare insurance, where premiums grew by 13.7% in 2022 and in 2024 by 12% – a double digit growth over the years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: It is projected to grow by another 12% this year, according to the Willis Towers Watson survey.

sections.label: Questions on medical inflation and 3Ms
sections.summary: The question asks the Minister for the current medical inflation rate and whether MOH will review the 3Ms system.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share with the House what is the current medical inflation rate?

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Will MOH carry out a review of the 3Ms system and see how they can further enhance the system to help Singaporeans?

sections.label: Healthcare budget growth figures
sections.summary: MOH's budget rose from $9 billion to $21 billion, is estimated over $30 billion by 2030, and a two-percentage point GST increase gives about $5 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The Ministry of Health (MOH) was very far behind at $9 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: This year's healthcare budget is $21 billion, moved to second behind the Ministry of Defence (MINDEF).

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: By 2030, it is estimated to be over $30 billion – at least another $10 billion increase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: In comparison, a two-percentage point increase in GST gives us about $5 billion more in revenue today.

sections.label: Doubling MediSave outpatient scan limit
sections.summary: The MediSave withdrawal limit for outpatient scans will double from $300 to $600 per year starting in 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: To ensure these remain affordable, we will double the MediSave withdrawal limit for such outpatient scans, from $300 to $600 per year, starting in 2026.

sections.label: Raising outpatient withdrawal limit
sections.summary: The withdrawal limit will increase to $400 per year from the fourth quarter of 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Since then, outpatient medical needs have grown further.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We will therefore increase the withdrawal limit to $400 per year, from the fourth quarter of 2025.

sections.label: Dental subsidies and Flexi-MediSave
sections.summary: CHAS dental subsidy limits for restorative procedures will increase for Pioneer and Merdeka Generation and CHAS Blue and Orange cardholders, and Flexi-MediSave can be used for costlier treatments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: This diminishes our ability to chew effectively and in our old age, affects our nutritional intake.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We will, therefore, increase the CHAS dental subsidy limits for restorative procedures, such as root canal, for Pioneer and Merdeka Generation as well as CHAS Blue and Orange cardholders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We will also allow Flexi-MediSave to be used for costlier treatments like root canals and permanent crowns at CHAS dental clinics and public healthcare institutions.

sections.label: Implementation in fourth quarter 2025
sections.summary: The enhancements and fee benchmarks will be implemented around the fourth quarter of 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Both the enhancements and fee benchmarks will be implemented around the fourth quarter of 2025.

sections.label: Subsidy increases and eligibility expansion

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: In short, we will, as indicated in blue, increase subsidies by five to 15 percentage points for almost all eligible households; expand eligibility for maximum subsidy of 75% to 80% from about two in 10 to about three in 10 households.

sections.label: Subsidy increases effective July 2026
sections.summary: The increases in subsidies will be effective from July 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The increases in subsidies will be effective from July 2026.

sections.label: Discounted fees capped by MOH
sections.summary: Instead of $1,300 a month, they pay a discounted amount of about $900 because MOH caps their fee increases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Instead of $1,300 a month, today they pay a discounted amount of about $900, because MOH caps their fee increases.

sections.label: Long-term care package for seniors
sections.summary: The long-term care enhancements will benefit more than 80,000 seniors, with support of up to $2.1 billion from 2025 to 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The entire package of long-term care enhancements will benefit more than 80,000 seniors, who can expect to receive support of up to $2.1 billion, from 2025 to 2030.

sections.label: Hospital bed capacity expansion
sections.summary: Over the past five years, capacity was expanded by over 6,300 beds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Over the past five years, we have expanded capacity by over 6,300 beds, as shown on the slide.

sections.label: Planned public hospital beds
sections.summary: From 2025 to 2030, 13,600 more beds are planned, bringing public hospital beds from 12,000 to 15,000 in 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: From 2025 to 2030, we plan to add another 13,600 beds to our system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: It will also include beds in the redeveloped Alexandra Hospital and the new Eastern General Hospital, which will open progressively from 2028 and 2029 respectively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: This will bring public hospital beds from 12,000 today to 15,000 in 2030.

sections.label: Healthcare staff and medical intake
sections.summary: Salary enhancements were announced for pharmacists, allied health, administrative and ancillary staff, medical school intake rose to 550, and recognised overseas universities were expanded.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Over Chinese New Year, I also announced salary enhancements for pharmacists, allied health professionals, administrative and ancillary staff later this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We have expanded the list of recognised overseas universities, so we can welcome more Singaporeans studying medicine overseas to return to Singapore to practice.

sections.label: Doctors' salary adjustments
sections.summary: Salary adjustments for doctors were implemented on 1 February 2024 to stay competitive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Thirdly, salary adjustments for doctors were implemented 1 February 2024 only recently and we try to make sure we are competitive.

sections.label: AI, genomics and genetic data
sections.summary: AI and genomics are driving a healthcare scientific revolution, and new legislative protections for genetic test information are being worked on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Technological breakthroughs, like AI and genomics, are ushering a scientific revolution in healthcare.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We are now working on new legislative protections to safeguard the use of genetic test information.

sections.label: Generative AI transcription adoption
sections.summary: By the end of this year, all public healthcare institutions are hoped to adopt generative AI systems that transcribe and summarise doctors' conversations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Where an application is workable and is effective, we will expand it throughout the healthcare system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Hence, by the end of this year, we hope all public healthcare institutions will adopt generative AI systems that can automatically transcribe doctors' conversations with their patients and summarise them for doctors' review before they are entered into patients' healthcare records.

sections.label: Flexi-MediSave, dental and long-term care subsidies
sections.summary: The withdrawal limit for Flexi-MediSave rises from $300 to $400 yearly, dental subsidies increase, Flexi-MediSave can pay for root canal treatments and dental crowns, and long-term care subsidies increase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Second, we are increasing subsidies for certain dental services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Singaporeans can now also use their Flexi-MediSave to pay for root canal treatments and dental crowns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Third, we are increasing subsidies for long-term care services.

sections.label: Singapore lifespan and healthspan
sections.summary: Singapore has one of the world's highest average lifespans at 84, but its healthspan is only 74.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Singapore, indeed, has one of the highest average lifespans in the world at 84, but our healthspan is only 74.

sections.label: Healthier SG enrolment numbers
sections.summary: After one and a half years, almost 1.2 million Singaporeans, about half of the eligible population, enrolled onto Healthier SG, and three-quarters of enrollees completed their Health Plan consultation.

sentences.text: After one and a half years, we enrolled almost 1.2 million Singaporeans onto Healthier SG, about half of the eligible population.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Three-quarters of our enrollees have also since completed their Health Plan consultation.

sections.label: Sugar, sodium, Grow Well SG, AI
sections.summary: Sugar consumption has been cut, including in the Members' Room, with moves soon to sodium and saturated fats, Grow Well SG was implemented, and AI models will analyse medical or genetic data to predict strokes, heart attacks or cancer 10 years ahead.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We have cut down sugar consumption, including in the Members' Room.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We are moving soon to sodium and saturated fats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We implemented Grow Well SG to improve health habits of our young.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: And at some point, AI models will analyse our medical or even genetic data to predict 10 years ahead if we are likely to get a stroke, heart attack or cancer.

sections.label: S+3Ms framework for medical care
sections.summary: Through the S+3Ms framework, no one will be denied appropriate medical care because they cannot afford it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Through our S+3Ms framework, we will ensure no one is denied appropriate medical care because they cannot afford it.

sections.label: Grow Well SG for children
sections.summary: Forty-eight new initiatives to support children and mothers were recommended, especially for vulnerable and at-risk groups, and MOH, MOE and MSF launched Grow Well SG in January, targeting children below 12.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Forty-eight new initiatives to support children and mothers were recommended, especially for vulnerable and at-risk groups.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: There is compelling evidence showing that poor lifestyle behaviours in childhood can impact children’s health and development, making early adoption of healthy habits crucial to their long-term health.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: This is why MOH, MOE and MSF launched Grow Well SG in January, a new population health effort to help children and families inculcate healthy lifestyles, with a stronger focus on preventive care, targeting children below 12 for a start.

sections.label: Health Plans for students
sections.summary: Personalised Health Plans with lifestyle prescriptions were introduced in January for Primary 1 to 3 students, with rollout to all such students by end-2025.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: In January, we introduced personalised Health Plans with lifestyle prescriptions for Primary 1 to 3 students.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: We are on track to roll out Health Plans to all Primary 1 to 3 students by end-2025.

sections.label: Childhood Health Behaviours Checklist rollout
sections.summary: The Childhood Health Behaviours Checklist is being rolled out at Childhood Developmental Screening visits for children up to six years from 2 May 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Beyond schools, we are rolling out the Childhood Health Behaviours Checklist (CHBC) at Childhood Developmental Screening visits for children up to six years at all polyclinics, general practitioners and paediatric clinics from 2 May 2025.

sections.label: Age Well SG funding
sections.summary: Age Well SG was rolled out to support seniors, including older women, with $3.5 billion set aside over the next decade.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Our national programme, Age Well SG, was rolled out to support our seniors, including older women, and $3.5 billion has been set aside over the next decade for this.

sections.label: Silver Guardians volunteering numbers

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: To date, we have more than 1,400 Silver Guardians volunteering at the Active Ageing Centres and are one step closer to achieving our goal of 2,400 Silver Guardians by 2028.

sections.label: Seniors enrolled in service

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Since its launch, over 200 seniors have enrolled in this service.

sections.label: Application details for companies
sections.summary: Interested companies can expect application details and a good practice guide from the second half of 2025 onwards.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Interested companies can look forward to the application details and good practice guide from second half of 2025 onwards.

sections.label: Productivity and Digitalisation Grant
sections.summary: The Productivity and Digitalisation Grant, launched in 2022, has supported over 200 projects and benefited 48 community care organisations.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: The Productivity and Digitalisation Grant, launched in 2022, is one such example, which has supported more than 200 projects across this sector, benefiting 48 community care organisations thus far.

sections.label: Standardised care assessment by 2026
sections.summary: By end-2026, all seniors needing long-term care can progressively expect standardised care assessment and a holistic long-term care plan coordinated across services.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: By end-2026, all seniors requiring long-term care services can progressively look forward to receiving the standardised care assessment and holistic long-term care plan coordinated across services.

sections.label: Family Medicine as specialty
sections.summary: The Specialists Accreditation Board approved Family Medicine as a specialty, and accreditation and training pathways are being worked out to recognise Family Physicians as specialists.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: The healthcare profession recognises the complexity of the work, the importance of our colleagues in primary care and that specialised training and experience is needed to perform this role well.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Hence, the Specialists Accreditation Board has approved for Family Medicine to be recognised as a specialty, on par with other specialties.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Together with the family medicine fraternity, we are now working out the accreditation and training pathways to recognise Family Physicians with advanced Family Medicine training and relevant experience as specialists.

sections.label: Healthier SG Chronic Tier expansion
sections.summary: By mid-2025, the Healthier SG Chronic Tier will include three MAF drug products, potentially reducing eligible patients' monthly out-of-pocket expenses.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: By mid-2025, we will expand the range of medications under the Healthier SG Chronic Tier, to include three Medication Assistance Fund (MAF) drug products for specific medication indications.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: For example, eligible patients requiring Evolocumab for very high cholesterol levels, or Familial Hypercholesterolemia, despite being on other cholesterol-lowering medications, could see their monthly out-of-pocket expenses reduced from over $230 to about $30-$60, depending on their means test status.

sections.label: Care Protocols for mental health

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Healthier SG Care Protocols for major depressive disorder and general anxiety disorder are being developed and will be rolled out next year.

sections.label: CREST and COMIT teams
sections.summary: As of December 2024, there were 86 CREST and 32 COMIT teams, including youth teams, in operation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: As of December 2024, there were 86 CREST and 32 COMIT teams, including the youth teams, in operation.

sections.label: Funding of community mental health services
sections.summary: CREST and COMIT community mental health services are fully funded by the Government with no out-of-pocket cost.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Community mental health services provided by CREST and COMIT are fully funded by the Government with no out-of-pocket cost.

sections.label: Training individuals in mental health support
sections.summary: Over 137,000 individuals, including religious leaders and volunteers, have been trained, exceeding the target.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: This is part of our ongoing effort to strengthen community-based mental health support networks.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We have exceeded our target, with over 137,000 individuals trained to date, including religious leaders and volunteers.

sections.label: National Mental Health Helpline and Textline
sections.summary: A National Mental Health Helpline and Textline service will launch in mid-2025 as a centralised first-stop touchpoint.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: To simplify the help-seeking process, we will launch the National Mental Health Helpline and Textline service in mid-2025 as a centralised mental health first-stop touchpoint.

sections.label: Workplace mental health initiatives
sections.summary: The Well-being Champions Network now consists of over 450 organisations representing 230,000 employees.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Government agencies and tripartite partners have implemented comprehensive workplace mental health initiatives like the Well-being Champions Network, which now consists of over 450 organisations representing 230,000 employees.

sections.label: Fair employment and workplace fairness
sections.summary: The Tripartite Guidelines uphold employment fairness, and Workplace Fairness legislation will prohibit discrimination based on mental health conditions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: The Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices upholds employment fairness through merit-based recruitment, restricting unnecessary mental health declarations and providing proper grievance handling processes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: These practices will be further strengthened by the Workplace Fairness legislation, which prohibits workplace discrimination based on mental health conditions.

sections.label: Guidelines and youth wellness centre
sections.summary: MOH will convene an expert group to develop guidelines, and an integrated wellness centre for youths, grovve, will open at *SCAPE.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: After consulting medical ethics experts and mental health service providers, MOH has decided to take a nuanced approach by convening an expert group to develop guidelines in this area.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: For the Singapore Children's Society, for example, in their work, they have found that consistent parental engagement and parental involvement in case planning and family sessions have achieved sustained positive results and supported long-term recovery.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We are also introducing "grovve", an integrated wellness centre for youths at *SCAPE at the end of this year.

sections.label: 24/7 youth crisis facility
sections.summary: A 24/7 facility expected to be operational in 2027 will provide intervention for youths in crisis, including suicidal behaviour or severe self-harm.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Expected to be operational in 2027, this 24/7 facility will provide intervention for youths in crisis, including those struggling with suicidal behaviour or severe self-harm.

sections.label: Registration of psychologists
sections.summary: Work is towards registering psychologists who provide direct patient care, perform higher-risk assessments and interventions, and may span various sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Recognising this shift, we are working towards the registration of psychologists, focusing on psychologists who provide direct patient care, perform higher-risk assessments and interventions, and whose practices may span across various sectors.

sections.label: HCSA advertising and health apps
sections.summary: HCSA advertising controls will be reviewed for selected professions, and public healthcare clinical apps will be consolidated into a unified platform by 2027.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Their interventions are low risk, because they manage conditions in accordance with clear standards of practice set by their professional bodies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We will review the HCSA advertising controls to enable these selected professions to advertise their services.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: To improve the online accessibility of public health care services, we are planning to consolidate the public healthcare clinical apps, Health Hub and the cluster-specific apps – Health Buddy, NHG Cares App and NUHS App – into a unified platform by 2027.

sections.label: Genetic testing and financing schemes
sections.summary: Genetic testing for familial hypercholesterolemia will be rolled out nationally in mid-2025, with Government financing schemes extended only to cost and clinically effective precision medicine use cases.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: One such application is genetic testing for familial hypercholesterolemia, which we will be rolling out nationally in mid-2025.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: To do so, we will only extend Government financing schemes, mainly subsidies, MediShield Life and MediSave, to precision medicine use cases that are assessed to be cost and clinically effective.

sections.label: Risks of investigational therapies
sections.summary: Risks and ethical considerations of nascent investigational therapies are recognised, and evidence from local and overseas studies will continue to be evaluated.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: However, we recognise the risks and ethical considerations associated with such nascent investigational therapies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We will continue to evaluate the evidence from both local and overseas studies for clinical efficacy and cost effectiveness.

sections.label: Nutri-Grade not applied to F&B
sections.summary: Nutri-Grade measures are not being applied to dishes in the F&B setting for now, as time is needed for consumers and operators to adjust.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Moreover, time is needed for consumers to adjust their palates to lower sodium dishes and for F&B operators to adopt healthier ingredients.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Therefore, we are not applying the Nutri-Grade measures to dishes in the F&B setting for now.

sections.label: HPB hawker centre outreach

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: HPB has reached out to 60 hawker centres, with 50 more planned for 2025.

sections.label: Eateries switching to lower-sodium ingredients
sections.summary: Over 1,700 eateries, including hawker centre stalls, have switched to lower-sodium ingredients, compared to 500 eateries two years ago.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Today, over 1,700 eateries, including stalls in hawker centres, have switched to lower-sodium ingredients, compared to 500 eateries two years ago.

sections.label: HPB community fitness programmes expanded
sections.summary: HPB's community physical activity programmes have expanded to over 2,100 weekly sessions, up from over 1,700 in 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: HPB conducts regular fitness programmes that are accessible and convenient for residents in the neighbourhoods.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: These community physical activity programmes have been expanded to over 2,100 sessions each week, up from over 1,700 sessions in 2023.

sections.label: Weekly attendance at fitness programmes

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Alongside the increase in physical activity programmes, the weekly attendances for these have increased from 36,000 participants in 2023 to 47,000 in 2024.

sections.label: Healthy 365 app enhanced
sections.summary: HPB enhanced the Healthy 365 app in October 2024, and more than 840,000 residents regularly use it.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: In response to user needs, HPB has also enhanced the Healthy 365 app with a new goal-setting feature and a refreshed set of milestone-based challenges in October 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Today, more than 840,000 residents regularly use the Healthy 365 app to track their progress in meeting their activity goals, access lifestyle activities, recommended resources and programmes, and earn rewards from completing tasks and challenges.

sections.label: Review of e-vaporiser legal penalties
sections.summary: MOH and HSA will review legal penalties to bolster deterrence against importation, distribution and use of e-vaporisers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Looking ahead, MOH and HSA will be reviewing legal penalties to bolster deterrence against the importation, distribution and use of e-vaporisers.

sections.label: Increase in number of partners
sections.summary: The number of partners rose from 100 in 2023 to over 160 in 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The number of partners has increased from 100 in 2023 to over 160 in 2024.

sections.label: Healthcare subsidies for foreign mothers
sections.summary: Foreign mothers married to Singapore Citizen fathers who are PRs or on LTVP+ can receive Singapore Citizen-level delivery subsidies and PR-level inpatient subsidies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: We understand that healthcare costs are an important consideration in setting up a family, particularly for transnational families.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Hence, foreign mothers who are married to Singapore Citizen fathers, and who are PRs, or on Long-Term Visit Pass Plus, LTVP+ in short, can receive Singapore Citizen–level subsidies for the delivery episode, in recognition that their child will be a Singapore Citizen and PR-level healthcare subsidies for all inpatient services.

sections.label: Subsidies for fertility preservation treatment

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: We agree that no one should have to forgo the opportunity to have a child because of the side effects from a medically necessary treatment for a condition.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Hence, from June this year, we will extend subsidies for embryo, egg and sperm freezing for those whose fertility can be irreversibly affected by their medical treatment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: From next year, we will also extend MediSave coverage for embryo freezing, and MediShield Life coverage to support embryo, egg and ovarian tissue freezing for such individuals.

sections.label: Nurse attrition rate in public healthcare

sentences.text: Today, the attrition rate of nurses in the public healthcare clusters has dropped from 9% during the pandemic years of 2021 to 2022 to around 6.7% in 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)

sections.label: Central procurement and bargaining power

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: For example, we now do central procurement and it gives us a bit more bargaining power, keeping prices low.

sections.label: HTA cost-effectiveness and drug subsidies
sections.summary: HTA ensures approved and subsidised treatments are cost-effective, with frank discussions with drug suppliers to lower costs, as with shingles vaccination.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, you have to really sharpen your pencil and calculate, and see if it is worth it and is it cost-effective.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, HTA has been set up as a discipline within MOH to make sure that whatever we approve and subsidise is cost-effective.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: If it is not cost-effective, we start to have very frank discussions with drug suppliers, for example, to tell them that they need to lower their cost, then we can subsidise, which was the case for shingles vaccination and that resulted in a good outcome.

sections.label: Fewer social stayers today
sections.summary: The number of social stayers today is far fewer, at 50 to 80.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Today, the numbers of social stayers are far fewer, 50 to 80.

sections.label: S+3Ms and co-payment restrain system

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, that is why we have S+3Ms, including co-payment, to restrain the system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, today we can deliver very good health outcomes at 5%, or, in fact, under 5% of gross domestic product.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: In fact, in the last two years, it was under 5%.

sections.label: No adjustment to $500 to $700
sections.summary: The $500 to $700 is not being adjusted yet.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As for Ms Hazel Poa's question, we are not adjusting the $500 to $700 yet.

sections.label: Increase from $300 to $400
sections.summary: The increase is from $300 to $400, after a 2021 increase from $200 to $300.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Therefore we review it and the increase from $300 to $400.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, if you look at what we have done, in 2021, it increased from $200 to $300; and now it increased from $300 to $400.

sections.label: Tracking mental health data
sections.summary: The coordinating office and new systems should help develop a framework to establish and track data across service providers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The ability to track such data in the past was limited.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Now that we have this coordinating office as well as the various systems that we are putting in place coming out of the strategy, it should allow us to then better develop the framework to establish that data across a variety of service providers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: So, we will be looking at this as part of how we set up and monitor the work of the National Mental Health Office, how to then get the right data and track it over time.

sections.label: Restorative treatment subsidy increase
sections.summary: The subsidy for restorative treatment is being increased significantly because of that behaviour.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, there is a bit of that behaviour.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: That is why we are increasing the subsidy for such restorative treatment quite significantly.

sections.label: Licensing psychologists and professionals
sections.summary: Higher-risk professionals involved in diagnosis, pathology and interventions may be regulated and licensed, with public education on choosing therapy.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The categories of psychologists and professionals that we are likely to then want to regulate and license in a particular way are those where their risk is likely to be higher to the clients and the patients that they are treating, that they are seeing.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: And this, by definition, means that they are involved in issues to do with diagnosis, pathology, interventions – this is the higher risk end of the profession.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Then, to her point where there are other professionals who are advertising or purporting to treat these types of problems with these types of interventions, we will have to look and see how we craft the licensing regime and the regulatory regime as to what tools we might then have to then go after such individuals.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: It is early days, but we are thinking in terms of the risks associated as a result of the professional work that someone does – the diagnosis, the risks and interventions – as well as the vulnerability of the individual that we want to protect.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Indeed, public education will be important, and we will have to think through how we set out the naming, the nomenclature and the details, how a member of the public can choose who to go and get their therapy from and then make available public information.

sections.label: Foreign spouses medical subsidies
sections.summary: Most foreign spouses with Singapore Citizen husbands and minor children are LTVP+ and eligible for medical subsidies, with few appeals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Based on the information that we have from the Immigrations and Checkpoints Authority, the vast majority of foreign spouses with Singapore Citizen husbands and have Singapore Citizen minor children are actually LTVP+.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: So, in that sense, the vast majority of spouses are therefore eligible for medical subsidies already.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: We generally receive very few appeals each year from Singapore residents for their sponsored dependants on LTVP.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: If you do have some of these cases, they can be surfaced, and they can approach medical social workers to request for MediFund.
